newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bankgesellschaft says Q1 oper profit up.
newsitem.headline: Bankgesellschaft says Q1 oper profit up.

text.p: Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG said on Monday its operating profit before risk provisions grew at a double-digit percentage rate in the first quarter of 1997 and predicted business would be satisfactory this year.

Germany's sixth-largest listed bank, which last week reported a slump in 1996 earnings caused by a large allocation to risk provisions, said its net interest and net commission income in the first quarter of 1997 matched the year-earlier levels.
Own-account trading profit in the first quarter had been well up from the year-earlier level, the bank said.

"Operating profit before provisions showed grew at a pleasing double-digit rate," Wolfgang Rupf, who took over as chief executive at the beginning of 1997, said in a statement released ahead of the bank's annual news conference.

The bank would become more efficient as a result of its move to clean up its loan portfolio and streamline its group structure, Rupf said. He added that the restructuring would be completed by mid-1997.
Bankgesellschaft last December announced it was setting aside 2.2 billion marks to cover problem loans amid an economic downturn in its home region of Berlin and east Germany.
As a result, its net profit in 1996 slumped to 47 million marks from 476 million while its operating profit after risk provisions fell to 355 million marks 958 million.
Before risk provisions, operating profit rose 5.6 percent to 1.78 billion marks last year.
